comparedAgainst: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Performance/Guides/How_browsers_work (MDN, fetched: ~3,500 words, three diagrams, one HTML sample, no runnable code; TLS and DNS covered in a few lines each)
https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mobile/what-happens-when-you-type-a-url-into-your-browser/ (AWS blog, fetched: ~2,500 words, screenshots, defers TCP/TLS to future posts)
justification: Presentation is at MDN level and the subject is better illustrated and better evidenced than in either comparison page: three figures that each carry information (Figure 1 sequence bands with RTT tags and an accent color for the encrypted flights, Figure 2 chunked-body byte accounting, Figure 3 layer wrapping with byte counts), all correct in dark theme and legible at 390 px (drawn on a 360-unit viewBox, annotations under the drawing). Rhythm for 5,850 words is good: prose, one program, an output panel, interpretation; three content-bearing callouts (In .NET, Note, Common pitfall), five exercises of different forms placed mid-flow with collapsed solutions, a compact timing table that fits at 390 px and is now labelled, one H1, specific H2s, H3s only under the long TCP and TLS sections, a 27-item dated Sources list. Output panels are 40 columns or less. Round-2 findings: the SNI-program clipping major is fixed (names array one per line, 'name' and 'options' arguments now on their own visible lines), British spellings fixed, the long H2 shortened, the table now has a label. Held below 8.5 for one visible copy defect and one unfinished job: the sentence about case-insensitive header names appears twice back to back in 'Where the response ends' (desktop-light part06, mobile-dark part09), and code-block tails are still under the phone fade on about eight blocks (details in issues; the operative token is visible in nearly every case, but IsFraming's '||' and the timing-table header row are not). Real numbers from report.json and lighthouse.json: Lighthouse 96/100/100/100 (FCP 2.3 s on the simulated mobile profile; flagged but non-blocking: unused CSS 13 KiB, document latency 173 KiB, bfcache), zero console errors, zero console warnings, zero broken links, mobileOverflowPx 0; the only failure is the expected NEEDS_MARKUS placeholder. Performance may be affected by other agents loading the machine at the time of the run; the orchestrator should re-measure serially. Not reviewable from screenshots: code inside the five collapsed exercise solutions.
